title: Product reviews in English only? You're losing 95% of buyers
description: Review channels live and die by reach. One review, 50+ languages — AI dubbing turns a local unboxing into a global sales conversation.
excerpt: The same iPhone review can sell in Berlin, Tokyo and São Paulo. Most reviewers never publish it there. AI dubbing changes that math.
content:
Product reviews are the most international genre on YouTube. The product is the same in every country. The specs don't change. The packaging doesn't change. Only the language does.

And that's exactly where most review channels stop. One language. Maybe two.

Here's the thing: a viewer in Germany doesn't watch your review to practice English. They watch it to decide whether to spend 1,200 euros. If they have to fight through subtitles, they leave and find a local reviewer. Your testing, your opinion — wasted on that market.

## Reviews travel better than any other format

Think about what a review video contains. Product shots — universal. Close-ups — universal. Price talk, spec talk, comparison talk — universal. The only language-bound part is your voiceover.

That's why dubbing works brutally well for reviews. You film once. You keep every cut, every angle, every demo. [TubeVoice](https://tubevoice.io) replaces just the voice — in 50+ languages, in hours, not weeks.

Compare that with travel vlogs or comedy, where humor and context die in translation. A review is pure information with a recommendation on top. Information translates.

## Unboxing is visual. Trust is verbal.

Unboxing videos are satisfying to watch on mute. But nobody buys because of the box. They buy because they trust your verdict.

Trust needs a voice. Your voice, ideally. Native viewers trust a speaker who sounds like one of them. [TubeVoice](https://tubevoice.io) offers voice cloning, so your channel sounds like you in every language — same tone, same energy, same catchphrases.

## Where the money hides

A $100-gadget review in English competes with a thousand other English reviews. The same review in Polish competes with maybe twenty. Ranking is easier. CPM in rich markets like Germany or Japan is higher. Affiliate links work in every language.

The math is simple: one video, times 50 markets, times your conversion rate. [TubeVoice](https://tubevoice.io) does the multiplying for you — and multi-voice dubbing keeps guest interviews natural when you collab with local creators.

## Start small, measure everything

Dub your five best-performing reviews first. Watch retention on the dubbed versions — it should match or beat the original. Then expand by category, not randomly. Tech reviews, gadget unboxings and audio gear are the safest bets: the audience is young, global and buys online.

One warning: don't settle for subtitles. Reviews are background-listening content. People watch them while cooking or commuting. Subtitles need eyes. Dubbing doesn't.

## The bottom line

Every review you publish in one language is a review 95% of the world never sees. [TubeVoice](https://tubevoice.io) closes that gap in hours.

Film once. Dub everywhere. Let the same verdict sell the same product to the whole planet.
